meta.title: The Journey
meta.description: How KUL Enterprises started. Jamaica, the Air Force, eleven years driving for other carriers, and the first truck of his own. The story behind the carrier in {location}.

setup: Ours began long before the first truck.
s01.heading: Every road has a beginning.

said: My mother brought my sister and me to America.
She told us we were spending the summer with our father.
s02.caption: Mark and his sister. Jamaica, early 1980s.
s02.lesson: Sometimes life's greatest journeys begin without our permission.

s03.turnA: While most kids spent their summers playing…
s03.turnB: Mine were spent on construction sites.
s03.coupletB: It's something to take pride in.
s03.lesson: Character is often built long before opportunity arrives.

stack: I wasn't satisfied with simply being told how things were.
I wanted to understand why they worked the way they did.
Questions became part of the journey.
Curiosity doesn't always give you immediate answers.
It gives you a lifetime of learning.
s04.lesson: Every road begins with a question.

s05.momentB: When someone else stops making the decisions.
s05.leaving: Leaving home wasn't just about finding a place to live.
s05.firstTime: For the first time, I was making my own decisions.
s05.cross: It was about finding out who I was.
s05.belonged: But every one of them belonged to me.
s05.couplet: Independence isn't the freedom to avoid mistakes. It's accepting responsibility for them.
s05.lesson: Growth begins the moment excuses end.

s06.freedomB: But freedom also brought a question.
s06.question: What kind of man did I want to become?
s06.airforce: That's what led me to the United States Air Force.
s06.noPhoto: No photograph exists of this decision
s06.lesson: Discipline isn't about being controlled. It's about learning to control yourself.

s07.lead: Some lessons can only be learned through discipline. It demanded:
s07.couplet: Discipline doesn't change who you are. It reveals who you're willing to become.

statements: I thought I knew where life was taking me.
But plans have a way of changing.
Life rarely asks whether you're ready.

cards: Opportunity has a way of finding people who are prepared for it.
I was learning to become dependable.
One opportunity led to the next.
Before long, I found myself leading others.
Leadership isn't about being in front.
It's about being someone others can count on.
s09.lesson: Trust is earned long before it's ever expected.

frames.line: I thought I was learning how to drive a truck.
What I didn't realize was that the road was teaching me something far greater.
Every mile introduced me to a new place.
Every state introduced me to different people.
Every delivery reminded me that trust travels farther than freight.
I had a plan. But plans have a way of changing.
There were victories. There were setbacks. Both became teachers.
I wasn't chasing titles. I was learning to become dependable.
The country was changing. And so was I.
Every load represented someone's trust. Every mile represented someone's promise.
The farther I traveled, the more I realized every person has a story.

s11.premise: Freight moved every day. But what truly kept the industry moving wasn't trucks.

roll.note: The only driver this archive has a picture of is the man who made it.
His own, in the only photograph of them.

s12.b1: There came a moment when I stopped asking:
s12.b2: what kind of business do I want to own?
s12.b3: I began asking a different question.
s12.b4: What kind of company deserves to exist?
s12.b5: A company built on honesty, when honesty costs something.
s12.b6: A company built on integrity, even when no one is watching.
s12.b7: I wasn't trying to build a trucking company.
s12.b9: I was trying to build something people could believe in.

s13.coupletB: But that's not where KUL began.
vows: To never compromise safety for convenience.
To remember that behind every shipment, every invoice, every phone call, is a person who placed their trust in us.
s13.lesson: Principles are promises you keep, even when they're difficult.

s14.say: We didn't build this company to be the biggest. We built it to be trusted.

s15.introB: Ours were learned… long before this company existed.

values.name: Integrity
values.promise: We do the right thing… even when no one is watching.

values.name: Safety
values.promise: Every load matters. Every person matters more.

values.name: Communication
values.promise: Trust grows when people know what's happening.

values.name: Respect
values.promise: We believe relationships are built… one conversation at a time.

values.name: Excellence
values.promise: Good enough has never been our destination.

values.name: Accountability
values.promise: When we make a promise… We intend to keep it.

s15.closeA: Values don't matter because they're written.

triad: Some journeys last a few miles.
stations: One promise kept at a time.
s16.still: KUL Enterprises is still writing its story.
s16.aheadA: We don't know every opportunity that lies ahead.
s16.aheadB: But we do know the principles that will guide us there.
s16.lesson: The journey never really ends. It simply becomes someone else's beginning.

summation: Every promise I've chosen to keep…
s17.turnA: Not because my journey is complete.
s17.turnB: But because it's finally ready… to serve yours.
s17.invite: Whenever you're ready… we'll be honored… to take the next one with you.
s17.colophon: This page is a record, not a brochure. Thirty-two plates from Mark Brown's own archive: twenty-four frames of road photographed through a windscreen over eleven years, two frames of Jamaica, three of a working life from 2021 to 2022, and three portraits. No photograph was staged, purchased, or generated. Three chapters of the story have no photograph at all, and the page says so rather than dressing the absence up.
s17.signoff: Thank you for taking this journey with us.
